title: Security review checklist: backup encryption + key handling (Redwood Private DR toolkit)
creator: Talia Benson
description:
Context
- We are close to piloting the Private backup/restore toolkit with 1–2 design partners. We need a consistent, auditable security review checklist for (a) backup encryption and (b) key handling across VPC + on-prem, including air-gapped.
- This checklist will be used by:
  - Security Eng (review/approval of implementation defaults)
  - GRC/Compliance (evidence expectations during customer security reviews)
  - Solutions + SRE (what to verify during pilots / restore drills)

Goals
- Produce a single checklist that is actionable for operators + internal reviewers.
- Make it explicit where Redwood has access vs where the customer retains exclusive control (KMS/HSM ownership boundaries).
- Define the minimum acceptable configuration for GA, and what qualifies as an exception.

Non-goals
- Not writing a full policy doc; this is a checklist + evidence capture requirements.
- Not defining product roadmap for a managed DR service.

Where this will live (deliverable)
- Confluence: security-and-compliance/risk-and-exceptions/private-backup-key-handling-guidance
- Cross-link from:
  - ADR-0137 (backup format + encryption)
  - Day-2 ops runbooks (backup create/verify + restore)
  - Release gate checklist (backup before upgrade)

Checklist (draft)
A) Key ownership + access boundaries
- [ ] Customer-owned encryption keys are supported (KMS/HSM where available) and are the default recommendation for enterprise.
- [ ] Redwood does not require plaintext access to customer master keys (document how envelope encryption / KMS works per backend).
- [ ] Clear operator guidance: which identity assumes which role (cluster role, backup job role, break-glass restore role).
- [ ] Least-privilege IAM (or equivalent) documented with example policies; no wildcard access to object storage prefixes beyond backup path.
- [ ] Break-glass role pattern documented:
  - separate role used only for restore
  - time-bound access procedure
  - audit trail requirements

B) Encryption at rest (backup artifacts)
- [ ] Storage backend encryption modes supported and documented:
  - S3 SSE-KMS (preferred) + SSE-S3 fallback
  - MinIO SSE (where deployed) and required server config
  - NFS/on-prem file repo: file-level encryption requirements (tooling supports encryption; keys stored outside backup payload)
- [ ] Backups are encrypted before leaving cluster when backend does not provide strong guarantees (e.g., NFS).
- [ ] Backup artifact format includes:
  - encryption metadata (algorithm, key id reference, version)
  - integrity metadata (checksums)
  - no secrets embedded in plaintext manifests

C) Encryption in transit
- [ ] Backup jobs use TLS to storage endpoints (S3/GCS/Azure/minio) and verify certs by default.
- [ ] For private endpoints / VPC gateways: document required DNS/TLS configuration.
- [ ] For air-gapped: document how we validate integrity when transport is via mounted repository / offline transfer.

D) Secrets / credentials handling
- [ ] Backup job credentials sourced from Kubernetes Secret with minimum scope; no credentials baked into images.
- [ ] Support for external secret managers where present (document patterns).
- [ ] No secrets written to logs (explicit redaction requirements + validation step).
- [ ] Rotation expectations:
  - KMS key rotation policy (customer-driven)
  - IAM creds (if static) rotation guidance

E) Audit logging + evidence
- [ ] Evidence checklist for customer security reviews (SOC2/ISO aligned):
  - screenshot/export of backup configuration (values.yaml / installer config) showing encryption mode + key reference
  - proof of last successful backup + checksum verification
  - object storage bucket policy / IAM role policy excerpt
  - KMS key policy excerpt demonstrating customer control
  - restore drill record (date/time, operator, outcome, RTO/RPO achieved)
- [ ] Audit logs emitted for:
  - backup create / verify / prune start+finish
  - restore start+finish
  - maintenance mode toggles
  - access denied / auth failures (without leaking creds)

F) Failure modes and safe defaults
- [ ] If encryption config is invalid/missing for selected tier, the tool fails closed with an actionable error.
- [ ] Document expected behavior when KMS is temporarily unavailable.
- [ ] Explicitly call out exception cases (e.g., “SSE-S3 allowed only for non-regulated tier”) and how to request approval.

G) Air-gapped/on-prem constraints
- [ ] Offline bundle handling does not leak key material; keys are provided out-of-band.
- [ ] Staging repository guidance includes access controls + at-rest encryption requirements.
- [ ] Size constraints and chunking/compression guidance included (avoid partial uploads; checksum verification required).

Acceptance criteria
- Checklist finalized and reviewed with:
  - Marcus Lin (Security Eng lead) as approver
  - Hanae Suzuki (Security Eng) for secrets/certs specifics
  - Olga Petrov (Compliance/GRC) for evidence requirements wording
- Checklist published to Confluence with a stable link.
- Runbooks updated to reference checklist steps (backup verify + restore preflight).
- Pilot readiness: Solutions (Markus Klein / Fatima Noor) confirm checklist is usable during customer security review and DR pilot.

Open questions
- Do we standardize on “customer-managed keys only” for regulated tier, or allow Redwood-managed keys with documented compensating controls?
- For NFS/offline repo: do we mandate client-side encryption always, or allow encrypted filesystems with evidence?

Links (to add/confirm)
- ADR: adr-0137-private-backup-format-and-encryption
- Confluence draft: private-backup-key-handling-guidance
- Related PRs: redwood-private-installer (rw-private-dr), redwood-terraform (KMS wiring), observability-pack (backup metrics/alerts)

Notes from initial review (2025-12-09)
- Olga: needs explicit “evidence artifacts” section (what to attach to customer security questionnaire) + retention guidance for those artifacts.
- Hanae: ensure we call out cert/private CA handling for on-prem object stores; document what happens when endpoint TLS uses a private CA.
- Marcus: require least-privilege example policies for restore role separately from backup role; break-glass needs audit requirements (ticket/approvals).
comments: 2025-11-21 (Marcus Lin): Drafting checklist based on ADR-0137 + current installer flags. Will send to Olga for evidence requirements before publishing.
2025-12-03 (Olga Petrov): Please add a section explicitly listing artifacts we expect customers to provide during audits (config snapshots, KMS key policy excerpt, last restore drill record).
2025-12-06 (Hanae Suzuki): Add guidance on private CA chains for MinIO/on-prem endpoints and confirm we are not logging any Secret values in debug mode.

2025-12-09 (Marcus Lin): Posted v0.9 to Confluence draft; requesting final review from Olga + Hanae. Next: ensure runbooks link to checklist and add least-privilege examples for separate backup vs restore IAM roles.
